questions.text: Examine external hull plating, topsides, waterline, and draft marks for corrosion, deformation, cracking, or marine fouling.
Check main deck plating, bulwarks, handrails, scuppers, and deck water-freeing arrangements for structural integrity and cleanliness.
Inspect mooring winches, windlasses, fairleads, bollards, and anchor chains for proper operation, lubrication, and brake holding.
Verify that RADAR, ECDIS, GPS, and AIS equipment are operational with authorized electronic chart updates and sensor inputs.
Test GMDSS communication consoles, emergency MF/HF and VHF radios, EPIRB, SART, and reserve emergency battery banks.
Check magnetic compass deviation card, gyro compass repeater synchronization, navigation lights, and sound signaling equipment.
Inspect main propulsion engine, auxiliary generators, and boilers for abnormal vibration, temperature, or oil/fuel/steam leakage.
Verify that bilge alarms, emergency bilge suction, and Oily Water Separator (OWS 15ppm) are fully operational with valid calibration.
Test steering gear power units, emergency helm control in the steering flat, rudder angle indicators, and low-oil level alarms.
Inspect lifeboats and rescue boat: check engine starting, davit falls, release gear on-load/off-load mechanism, and onboard inventory.
Examine inflatable life rafts, hydrostatic release units (HRUs), lifebuoys with lights/smoke markers, and immersion suits.
Test emergency fire pump, international shore connection, fire main hydrants, hoses, nozzles, and emergency fire flaps.
Inspect cargo hold hatch covers, compression bars, rubber packing, hydraulic cleating, and drain channels for weathertightness.
Examine cargo hold internal structures: frames, brackets, ladders, bilges, and bilge suction strainers for damage and cleanliness.
Verify ballast tank air vents, flame screens, sounding pipe caps, and remote ballast valve control indicators are in working order.
